name: Red Oak Natural 3/4" Solid
description: Classic 3/4" solid red oak — the most popular hardwood in America. Can be sanded and refinished multiple times over its lifetime. Install in dry areas only; not recommended for basements or bathrooms.
notes: Requires acclimation 48–72 hrs before installation. Nail-down or glue-down only.

name: White Oak Engineered 1/2"
description: White oak's cooler, straighter grain is the designer's choice. Engineered 1/2" construction handles humidity swings better than solid wood — suitable over radiant heat and on grade in dry climates.
notes: Can be floated, stapled, or glued. Compatible with most radiant heat systems under 85°F.

name: Hickory Wire-Brushed Engineered
description: Wire-brushed surface brings out the natural character and dramatic grain variation of hickory. The textured finish hides everyday scratches and is easier to maintain than a smooth surface.
notes: Wire-brushed texture is very forgiving — great choice for homes with dogs or active kids.

name: Brazilian Cherry (Jatoba) Solid 3/4"
description: One of the hardest, most exotic hardwoods available. Rich reddish-brown color deepens over time with light exposure. Exceptional durability — outlasts most domestic species.
notes: Color will darken significantly in the first 6 months. Use window coverings to control UV exposure during this period.
